summary: Describes a new series of documents, Best Current Practices, that carry the endorsement of the IESG. It is now historic.

eli5.summary: Announces a new kind of document that says here is how the experts currently do things well.

questions: what is the best current practice series
can a bcp become an internet standard
subtitle: The memo that created the Best Current Practice (BCP) series of IESG-endorsed RFCs.

tldr.problem: The IETF had standards track documents and informal RFCs, but no way to publish relevant technical information that it endorses.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 1818 creates a new subseries of RFCs called Best Current Practices (BCPs), reviewed by the IESG with a last call, and published once the IESG approves.
tldr.outcome: A BCP has the technical approval of the IETF but cannot become an Internet Standard. This RFC is now listed as Historic.

today: RFC 1818 is listed as Historic, and no replacement is recorded in the unit metadata. It describes how the BCP series was first set up in August 1995.

sections.title: The Gap Before BCPs
sections.content:
The IETF process had two kinds of RFCs: standards track documents, which lead to an official Internet Standard, and other RFCs such as informational ones, experimental ones and FYIs.

Informational RFCs are published on a less formal basis, are not subject to peer review and, in the memo's words, carry no significance whatsoever within the IETF process. The IETF had no other means of publishing relevant technical information that it endorses.
sections.eli5: There were official rulebooks and casual notes, but nothing in between for "we agree this is a good way to do it".

sections.title: The BCP Subseries
sections.content:
The memo creates a new subseries called Best Current Practices. Documents in the series carry the endorsement of the Internet Engineering Steering Group (IESG). This RFC is itself BCP 1.

The process is similar to that for proposed standards. The document goes to the IESG for review and the existing review process applies, including a last call on the IETF announcement mailing list.
sections.eli5: A BCP gets checked by the same group of reviewers as other important documents, and the public gets a chance to comment first.

sections.title: How a BCP Is Approved
sections.content:
Once the IESG has approved the document, the process ends and the document is published. There is no further maturity ladder.

The result is viewed as having the technical approval of the IETF, but it is not, and cannot become, an official Internet Standard. The memo suggests "OSI NSAP Allocation" and the "OSPF Applicability Statement" as possible examples of subjects for BCPs.
sections.eli5: After the reviewers say yes, it is published and finished. It is a trusted guide, but it never becomes an official standard.
